Ablation: A comparison that changes or removes a component to test its role; resource changes can confound it.
Calibration: Agreement between predicted probabilities and observed event frequencies in a stated population.
Collapse: A representation loses useful distinctions, often by mapping different inputs to the same or nearly identical vectors.
Data leakage: Information unavailable at the intended prediction time influences fitting or evaluation.
Idempotency: Repeating the same operation with the same identity has the same intended effect as performing it once.
Latent representation: A learned internal description of an input; its coordinates need not have direct physical meaning.
Operator: A mapping between functions, generally observed through sampled discretizations in an ML dataset.
Point-in-time data: Information constrained to what was actually available at a historical decision time.
Provenance: The recorded origin, version, permissions, transformations, and identity of an artifact.
Rollout: A sequence generated by repeatedly applying a transition or prediction rule, often feeding predictions back as inputs.
Surrogate: A model approximating a more expensive process or computation within a specified scope.
Policy: A rule or distribution for choosing actions from available information.
